why: A puts the reason and the result in the same beat ('The base matches the number inside. So the answer is one.'); B splits that into two beats and spends a whole beat on 'The answer is one.' after already saying it, and B's 'five times six gives log base three of thirty' skips 'is thirty'.
notes: Beat 3: the margin note '← Plus means multiply' lands on 'log base three of thirty', about a second after the voice says 'Plus means multiply'. Acceptable (the note sits near ab, which only appears on 'Five times six'), but it is a lag.
Beat 3 carries a new line and a note — two new things, at the limit.
Neither draft uses his law names (Add Power / Minus Power). 'Plus means multiply, minus means divide' is also his wording, so not a fault; a later laws clip could name them.
Beat 4 trap ('Log five times log six is not log thirty') is plain, said once, right after the combine where it bites.
